responses.review_design:1:1: fixed: section 6 is rewritten as an exact contract against G1039 rev 1 §5 items 1-6: carry.unchanged(ident, node, key, old_cp, new_cp, scope) -> bool; records.checkpoint_scope(graph, node, record) -> list|None, derived from record.frozen and never stored (no checkpoint scope key); Identity.change(base, commit, paths=None) with G1039 adding unified=3; base output key synced = {old, onto, work, tip, merge, resolved} (null when the base did not move and in rebase mode); carry.relocate(cp, synced); previous.interdiff as git log -p --first-parent --no-merges plus previous.syncs (remerge-diff per merge). It ends with the list of edits G1039 makes (unchanged signature, no scope key, synced.old not sync.from, the interdiff form) for the root to relay.
responses.review_design:1:2: fixed: 4.5.1 defines own(W, P) as rev-list --first-parent --no-merges W ^P ^<second parent and Zzzops-Old-Base trailer of every merge on the first-parent chain>, minus docs(review) commits. Each engine sync merge carries the Zzzops-Old-Base: <B0> trailer (4.1, 4.8). Test 6 covers a dropped dependency, a rewritten dependency head and a dev-to-release/N target change, and asserts c2's subject and body list only the goal's commits (a dev feat! does not add !).
responses.review_design:1:3: fixed: 4.5.2 ranks by release effect from release.config.cjs (feat > fix/perf/revert > most common no-release type > chore; ! for any breaking implementation commit), over implementation commits only (an own commit is a tests commit iff its type is test and it touches only F). c1 is always test:. Test 5 covers revert + refactor giving revert, and test_design commits never deciding c2.
responses.review_design:1:4: fixed: R1 is restated truthfully: building on base_commit is today's behaviour (integrate rebuilds on ctx.inputs base); the base does not always re-sync before integrate; the PR tree equals the tested tree; if trunk moved, CI on the PR and GitHub's mergeability (CONFLICTING/BEHIND, turned into base findings by G1021) cover it. Outcome §1 and test 5 say 'on the trunk commit of the last sync (today's behaviour)', and R1 states that this is how acceptance 3's 'trunk tip' is met.
responses.review_design:1:5: fixed: D9, 4.1 and section 8 make it a precondition: the new engine writes merge syncs only when settings.engine.requires contains merge_sync; until then base keeps today's rebase (synced null, replay_map, today's carry). Requiring the capability pauses older engines (G1027), so no older engine ever runs base on a merged branch. The false 'fails closed' claim is removed. Test 8 covers both modes and the pause. Blocking base instead was rejected (section 11) because it would stop every sync in the window.
responses.review_design:1:6: fixed: the resume (4.2) refuses when git status --untracked-files=all shows any path outside the listed files (re-blocks listing them), and then stages only the listed files with git add -A --literal-pathspecs -- <files>. Test 1 covers an untracked scratch file, a *.orig file and an edit to a non-listed file.
responses.review_design:1:7: fixed: adopted the owner's decision, recorded verbatim in 2.1, in 4.8 and D10. Covered: every commit on work, stack and PR branches, agent- and engine-made. Exempt: record commits on goal refs (zzzops: answer G<g> ..., parsed by G1026) and lease refs, because they are machine-parsed and never reach trunk. Submit refuses non-conventional subjects (commit_subject) and non-test commits from the preserved node (test_commit_type), and implement commits touching frozen paths (test_freeze, now per commit); codes, texts and the SPEC §4.14 text are given. Engine subjects become chore(sync): merge <onto> into G<g> and chore(stack): combine/partial combine for G<g>; integrate's commits are test: and the derived type (4.5.2). Test 10 covers both refusals and the engine subjects; test 5 covers the type derivation.

output.summary: Revision 2 keeps the merge-tree sync with an explicit merge base, the frozen-path scoping of the tests checkpoint and the two-commit tree-overlay squash, and fixes all seven findings. The merge sync is now gated on the policy requiring merge_sync (base keeps rebasing until then), the conflict resume stages only the listed files, the goal's own commits exclude every previous base via a Zzzops-Old-Base trailer, and c2's type is ranked by release effect over implementation commits only. It adopts the owner's conventional-commit rule (new submit refusals commit_subject and test_commit_type, per-commit test_freeze, chore(sync)/chore(stack) engine subjects, goal/lease record commits exempt), gives the squashed commits strictly increasing dates after any earlier PR head, and pins section 6 as an exact contract (unchanged, checkpoint_scope, relocate, change(paths), synced, interdiff/syncs) for G1039 to adopt.

findings.text: §6 answers an older G1039 draft, and four of G1039 rev 1's six §5 items don't match. (1) G1039 calls unchanged(node, old_cp, new_cp) and reads 'the checkpoint's recorded scope'; G1038 defines clean(node, k, r, cp2, scope) with the scope from checkpoint_scope(graph, node, record). (3) G1039 relies on a stored checkpoint scope key, which D3 rejects, so G1039's predicate would always run unscoped and stale test_design whenever implementation lines move. (4) G1039 reads base output sync = {from, onto, merge, resolved}, including sync.from in §3.4; G1038 writes synced = {old, onto, work, tip, merge, resolved}. (6) G1039 describes the interdiff as 'range-diff plus previous.syncs'; G1038 drops range-diff for log -p --first-parent --no-merges plus previous.syncs. §6's left column also quotes needs G1039 rev 1 no longer has (relocate(node, key, cp, synced); Done.synced = {old, onto, tip}). Fix: rewrite §6 against G1039 rev 1 §5 items 1-6; pin one name, signature and key set (for example unchanged(node, k, old_cp, new_cp, scope), with the scope passed in from checkpoint_scope and never stored, and output key synced with old); state the exact edits G1039 must make (no scope key, synced.old not sync.from, the interdiff form) so the root can relay them. Otherwise two goals that each pass review are built against a carry interface neither one implements.

The own-commit walk P..W (§4.5: c2's type and '!', the body's subjects, the BREAKING CHANGE footers, authors and dates) picks up foreign commits whenever onto does not descend from the old base. That happens with a rewritten dependency PR head (routine under G1038, since every re-integrate re-squashes the PR branch), a dropped dependency, or a G1025 target change. D1 keeps the tree right, but M = commit-tree -p tip -p onto keeps the old base in first-parent history, so log --first-parent P..W walks into old dependency commits, or into all dev history not on release/N. Example: a dev 'feat!:' lands in a hotfix's c2 and forces a major bump on the line. Fix: exclude every previous base, not just P. For example, record the old base as a trailer in each engine merge message, then walk --first-parent --no-merges W ^P ^<each merge's second parent> ^<each recorded old base>. Add test-6 cases that assert the c2 subject and body.

c2's type derivation does not match release.config.cjs, so 'semantic-release computes the same release bump' is false in some cases. revert releases a patch, but the order 'feat > fix > perf > any other > chore' puts revert in an unordered 'other' bucket, so a revert: + refactor: goal can get refactor: and no release. The walk also counts test_design's commits (test:, fix(test):). Fix: rank by release effect (breaking > feat > fix/perf/revert > no release); derive c2's type from implementation commits only (those touching paths outside F, the split §4.5 already uses for identity); c1 is always test:. Test the revert case.

R1's premise is factually wrong. Outside branching mode nothing re-syncs base when dev moves (G1025 §2: G1021 keeps base non-stale on dev moves), and in branching mode G1025 pass 3 fires only before agent phases of unstacked goals, never before ops (G1025 §5.3, D1). So 'at integrate time, in the normal flow, the last synced trunk commit is the live tip' does not hold, and the PR routinely sits on an older trunk commit. The conclusion is still defensible: today's integrate already rebuilds on ctx.inputs['base'], the PR tree equals the tested tree, PR CI and GitHub check the real merge, and BEHIND/CONFLICTING come back to base. Fix: restate R1 with that reasoning; reword outcome §1 and test 5 to 'on the trunk commit of the last sync (today's behaviour)', and say explicitly that this is how acceptance 3's 'trunk tip' is met.

§8 and D9 claim an older engine 'would refuse a work branch with merges (I1/I2) ... fails closed'. That is false for base. At dev, base.py runs wt.sync, then 'rebase -q --onto onto old', which drops the merges and replays the pre-sync commits (redoing their conflicts); then check_i1_i2(onto, H) on the linearised result, which passes; then a non-fast-forward push (W, H), the rewrite this goal removes. Old agent submits also pass, because check_i1_i2(W, head) covers only the agent's own range. Only an old integrate fails closed. Workers here run cached plugin engines, so this window is real. Fix: make the policy step a precondition. Either the new engine writes a merge sync only when settings.engine.requires contains merge_sync (otherwise base blocks with a policy-prerequisite item), or state the rule that the merge_sync policy lands before the first merge-synced base runs. Correct §8 and D9, and add a test.

The conflict resume (§4.2) runs 'git add -A', so anything in the worktree goes into the merge commit, and from there into the goal's code and its squashed PR: untracked scratch files, *.orig files from mergetool, build output, edits to files that did not conflict. Fix: stage only the listed files (git add -A -- <files>); re-block if any other path differs from T, listing those paths, and refuse untracked or modified files outside the list. Cover this in test 1.

Owner decision, relayed by the root (material). Owner, verbatim: "Yeah, we should ensure we always use conventional commit messages". This was in reply to the root's proposal: keep the tests/implementation split by recorded frozen paths and per-phase submit ranges, not by commit message; (1) submit refuses commits whose subjects are not conventional commits, test_design's commits must be test:, and implement's commits must not touch frozen paths; (2) integrate's squashed tests commit is 'test: ...' and the implementation commit's type is derived from the goal's commits. The design must adopt this and state which commits the rule covers. The root recommends: every commit on work and PR branches, agent-made and engine-made (docs(review): commits already comply); engine record commits on goal refs ('zzzops: answer G<g> ...', which G1026 parses) keep their machine subjects because they never reach trunk; justify any other scope. G1038's own engine commits do not comply: the sync merge 'Merge <onto> into zzzops/work/g<g> (zzzops base)' (§4.1), and the combine commits 'zzzops: stack for G<g> ...' / 'zzzops: partial stack' (base.py combine) on the stack branches PRs target. Give them conventional subjects (for example chore(sync): ..., chore(stack): ...) or exclude them with a reason. Add the submit refusal codes and texts, the SPEC §4.14 text, tests for both refusals and for the engine subjects, and the type derivation from the implementation commits' conventional types.

output.summary: The core mechanism is sound: a merge-tree sync with the old base_commit as merge base, a read-tree conflict checkout, the preserved checkpoint scoped to its frozen paths, a tree-overlay squash, and no fingerprint change on upgrade. Seven findings block approval: §6 does not match G1039 rev 1 §5 (name, signature, a stored scope key, the synced/sync keys, the interdiff form); the own-commit walk P..W includes foreign commits when onto does not descend from the old base; c2's type derivation does not follow the release rules (revert) and counts test commits; R1's premise is wrong; the claim that old engines fail closed is false for base; the resume's git add -A absorbs stray files; and the owner's conventional-commit decision is not yet in the design.

spec:
Found while dogfooding Release 1. Two pieces of machinery caused most of the friction in the G1022–G1028 run:
- Syncing a goal with the integration branch is a rebase. Conflict resolutions are not kept, so each later rebase redoes them, and a rebase rewrites the work branch.
- The frozen tests are the diff up to the tests checkpoint, and the implementation is everything after it, so a test fix found after implement has to be inserted before the implementation commits. That needs a history rewrite and a force-push of the work branch, which only the owner could run. It happened four times (G1025, G1026, G1027 twice).

Owner decisions (verbatim):
- "For updating the branch with the trunk, I think merges might work better as conflict resolution doesn't get lost. Then maybe a final rebase when integrating in order to clean up the history?"
- On the integrate history, the owner chose "Squash to tests + code" over rebasing with reused resolutions or keeping the merges: integrate collapses the goal into two commits (tests, implementation) on the trunk tip.
- "I think we may as well get these done now, before dogfooding again"

Scope:
- `base` (and any scheduled sync) brings trunk into the goal's work branch with a merge commit, never a rebase or force-push. A conflicting merge becomes a base finding as G1021 does today.
- test_design may add tests commits after implementation commits. Which tests are frozen, and which diff is the implementation, are computed from paths and checkpoints rather than commit order, so no history rewrite is ever needed during a goal.
- integrate produces the PR branch as exactly two commits on the integration tip: the goal's tests and its implementation (plus the review records the engine already carries, if they must stay separate). The work branch is left as is.
- No owner-run force-push is needed at any point in a goal's normal flow.

Acceptance:
- A goal whose trunk moves twice during delivery syncs by two merges; the second sync does not redo the first sync's conflict resolution.
- A test fix submitted by test_design after implement committed is accepted without any rewrite; implement may not edit it; review_impl sees only implementation changes.
- The PR for such a goal has exactly the tests commit and the implementation commit on the trunk tip, and its tree equals the work branch merged with trunk.
- This PR edits docs/design/SPEC.md and DESIGN.md for every contract change it makes and adds a HISTORY §4 row.
title: Sync goal branches with trunk by merge, squash at integrate, and let test fixes land after implementation
